title: Nonzero-charge matter-density cylinder compatibility on the stable strip

parents.composition_rule: This is a separately versioned researcher-owned extension. It does not edit, supersede or retroactively complete PAH-001, PAH-OMC-001, PAH-OMC-004 or PAH-OMC-005.

exact_scope.carrier_family: The PAH-OMC-004 two-row strip G_n. The first two squares are already split in G_2; G_3 splits the next frontier square, so the anchor-neighbour interaction closure is stable for this comparison.
exact_scope.anchors: a=(0,0) is the retained matter-density observable anchor; O and C are the strip anchors and no nontrivial anchor automorphism is used.
exact_scope.comparison: The exact finite comparison is the neutral coordinate inclusion J_(2,3): G_2 -> G_3. Level 1 is retained only as a deliberately checked boundary control, where the newly introduced d1 edge can touch the matter neighbour b and is not assumed compatible.
exact_scope.state_domain: The audited finite states have one radial occupation quantum placed at exactly one of the four anchor-patch vertices a,b,c,d, zero radial occupation on remote vertices, all four patch phases in Z_2, all five patch links in Z_2, and all patch aperture bits. Thus Q=1 is nonzero and the state count is explicit.
exact_scope.functional: Evaluate exactly the displayed PAH-001 F_rho: aperture onsite and matter polynomial, aperture edge stiffness, covariant matter edge term, and plaquette Wilson term. No term or coupling is added.
exact_scope.moves: Use the unchanged PAH radial-transfer roots along directed edges. For f(x)=ell_a, only directed roots on h00, v0 and d0 can change the observable; every phase, link, aperture and remote radial root has zero observable increment and is retained only by the full generator definition.
exact_scope.observable: The common cylinder is f(x)=ell_a, and the audit also records the bounded indicator 1_{ell_a=1}. Both are gauge invariant and anchor preserving because the gauge action changes phases/links but not radial occupation, and the anchor automorphism group is the identity.
exact_scope.normalization: Finite counting-measure Gibbs midpoint rates exactly as in PAH-001; no averaging over dropped variables is used. A radial root carries mobility m=(s_v s_w)^(nu/2), represented exactly by its squared mobility and midpoint exponent.
exact_scope.limit: No cutoff, volume, lattice, continuum, phase, beta or observation limit is taken. n is only a finite geometric refinement label.

maps.geometric_inclusion: J_(2,3) retains every G_2 vertex, edge, aperture, phase, radial occupation and link coordinate by geometric ID; new G_3 coordinates are appended with neutral aperture, zero radial occupation and neutral Z_2 labels. Since the old state has Q=1, J preserves Q.
maps.local_restriction: For radial roots incident to a, the affected-term closure contains the endpoint onsite terms, all aperture-stiffness and covariant-edge terms incident to either endpoint, and all Wilson faces meeting those terms. This closure is identical in G_2 and G_3; the G_1 -> G_2 boundary is an explicit control failure because d1 is newly incident to b.
maps.observable_lift: I_(2,3)f is the same pointwise coordinate cylinder f(ell_a) on both finite state spaces; it is not a conditional expectation and is defined on every fine state.
maps.root_correspondence: Each directed radial root on h00, v0 or d0 has the same admissibility, endpoint apertures, exact energy increment and observable increment in G_2 and G_3. All other roots have zero increment on f and 1_{ell_a=1}.

compatibility_proposition.statement: For every audited Q=1 patch state, the complete list of nonzero radial-transfer contributions to the generator of f=ell_a is identical under the neutral inclusion J_(2,3). Equivalently, the rootwise midpoint tuples (edge, direction, DeltaF, mobility^2, Delta ell_a, rate exponent) agree exactly. The same holds for the indicator 1_{ell_a=1}. The level-1 to level-2 comparison is not included in the proposition and is checked as a nonzero-boundary-defect control.
proof_obligations: A radial move incident to a changes only its two endpoint matter values; the full PAH energy difference is therefore computed without dropping endpoint onsite, edge, or face terms.
For G_2 and G_3 the endpoint closure for h00, v0 and d0 has the same edge/face incidence; the newly split frontier at column 2 is disjoint from that closure.
The radial mobility depends only on endpoint apertures and the midpoint exponent is recomputed from the exact full-energy difference.
The neutral inclusion preserves Q=1 and every retained patch coordinate, so each valid directed root has a fine counterpart.
The G_1 -> G_2 control has a changed d1 edge at b and must exhibit a nonzero matter-transfer defect for at least one state; this prevents premature extension of the stable range.
compatibility_proposition.cumulative_consequence: The matter-density cylinder has zero geometric generator defect for this finite G_2 -> G_3 comparison. No supremum over all cylinders, volumes, regulators or limit parameters is asserted.

finite_acceptance.primary: Enumerate every fixture state, evaluate the full PAH energy before and after each directed anchor-incident radial transfer on G_2 and G_3, compare rootwise tuples, and verify the G_1 boundary control.
finite_acceptance.independent: Rebuild the strip, matter values, all PAH energy terms, directed radial roots and midpoint tuples from direct formulas without importing the primary implementation.
finite_acceptance.hostile: Reject source drift, Q=0 substitution, omitted frontier terms, premature G_1 -> G_2 extension, fitted rates, wrong mobility, charge-changing inclusion, conditional averaging and physical promotion.
finite_acceptance.lean: Cross-check the exact charge, state count, stable endpoint closure, mobility products, midpoint factor and explicit n=1 boundary defect. Lean is a finite arithmetic cross-check, not a global theorem formalization.

known_boundaries.boundary_control: The G_1 -> G_2 matter-cylinder comparison is intentionally not claimed: the newly present d1 edge changes the covariant matter term when the quantum occupies b. This is a local failure boundary, not a refutation of later stable levels.
known_boundaries.local_only: The proposition covers f=ell_a and its indicator on one Q=1 finite strip fixture. It does not cover arbitrary matter, link or radial cylinders, or a global common algebra.
known_boundaries.fixture_only: Q=1, K=2, M_s=M_psi=1 and the displayed unit couplings are a finite researcher fixture. No parameter-uniform theorem is claimed.
known_boundaries.no_global_uniformity: Exact rootwise equality at G_2 -> G_3 does not establish a regulator-, volume- or source-uniform interaction estimate, an infinite-volume generator, or an ordered limit.
known_boundaries.no_physics: The Markov time and Q=1 sector are not quantum time, a physical sector, a vacuum, Pre-A, spacetime, gravity, QFT, Yang--Mills, a continuum or a mass gap.

non_claims: This contract is a researcher proposal, not an external source or physical authority.
The finite Q=1 result is not retroactive evidence that PAH-001 already contained this refinement map.
The G_1 boundary defect and G_2 -> G_3 equality are finite local statements, not a global common-core or uniform theorem.
No physical Pre-A, spacetime, event horizon, gravity, QFT, Yang--Mills, continuum, mass-gap, cosmic-origin or TOE conclusion follows.
No static fit selects the dynamics, and Markov time is not quantum real time, proper time or Lorentzian time.
single_next_question: Can a finite common-core class containing several matter and link cylinders be proved stable for all sufficiently interior strip levels, with a source-authorized uniform interaction bound rather than one cylinder at one fixture?
revisit_condition: Reopen the broader uniform lane only after a separately hashed owner contract supplies multiple-cylinder root transport, nonzero-Q state transport beyond the fixture, a common invariant core and a regulator/volume-uniform estimate in the declared limit order.
